dialect.guess: Micro Focus COBOL (likely RM/COBOL or Micro Focus with ACUCOBOL-GT screen handling)
evidence: ACCEPT ... LINE ... POSITION ... SIZE ... TAB UPDATE NO BEEP CURSOR ... ON EXCEPTION EXC-KEY (screen I/O syntax typical of Micro Focus / ACUCOBOL-GT)
DISPLAY ... LINE ... POSITION ... SIZE (screen DISPLAY syntax)
USE AFTER ERROR PROCEDURE ON CONTRAT (DECLARATIVES section)
READ CONTRAT PREVIOUS NO LOCK (ISAM-style file I/O with PREVIOUS and NO LOCK)
EVALUATE / END-EVALUATE, END-IF, END-READ (COBOL-85 scope terminators)
COPY statements for multiple copybooks (.CPY, .REC, .FC, .FDE, .NXX extensions)

purpose.summary: This program handles the printing/generation of 'entrée' (entry/contract) documents for personnel records. It presents an interactive screen to the user to select parameters (person type, status, cost centre, re-edition flag, signatory), then iterates over contract and personnel records to produce output via a dynamically-called model program (e.g. 'DEF' or 'DESP').

notable_features: ACUCOBOL-GT runtime call C$RERR for extended file error status
Screen I/O using ACCEPT/DISPLAY with LINE/POSITION/SIZE/TAB/UPDATE/NO BEEP/CURSOR clauses
ISAM-style sequential file navigation with READ PREVIOUS NO LOCK and START KEY <
Dynamic CALL using variable MODELE (set to 'DEF' or 'DESP') for pluggable report model
DECLARATIVES section with USE AFTER ERROR PROCEDURE
Extensive use of COPY statements for copybooks (.REC, .CPY, .FC, .FDE, .NXX)
LINKAGE SECTION with PROCEDURE DIVISION USING (subprogram interface)
French-language identifiers and comments (ENTREE, CONTRAT, CARRIERE, PRESENCE, etc.)
GO TO used within named paragraphs for loop control (READ-PERSON, CONTRAT-1)
verdict.notes: The file is clearly production COBOL from a French HR/payroll application. The screen handling syntax (ACCEPT ... TAB UPDATE NO BEEP CURSOR, CALL 'C$RERR') strongly suggests ACUCOBOL-GT or a compatible Micro Focus variant. The duplicate WHEN 4 clause in the EVALUATE block (lines ~155-165) appears to be a copy-paste bug in the source. Decoded with latin-1, consistent with French accented characters in box-drawing comment headers.
